sections.h2: What should a seller know about Kendall County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Kendall County is a small, fast-growing county in the Chicago area, with Yorkville as county seat and Oswego as its most populous village. It was formed in 1841 out of LaSalle and Kane Counties and covers 322 square miles, with the Fox River running through the northwest. Most residents live in the northeast and along that river, while the south stays largely agricultural.

Population went from 54,544 in 2000 to 114,736 in 2010 and 131,869 in 2020, and Census QuickFacts estimates 145,470 for July 2025, a 10.3 percent rise over the 2020 base. The county touches DeKalb, Kane, DuPage, Will, Grundy and LaSalle Counties, and it holds pieces of Aurora, Joliet, Montgomery and Plainfield along with Plano, Sandwich, Minooka, Newark and Lisbon. Two moraines cross at Oswego Township and raise some northern ground above 800 feet.

sections.h2: Which Kendall County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Three county offices and the township assessors share the work, and the county lists 504 S. Main St in Yorkville, IL 60560 for the Treasurer and the assessment office. Offices close for county holidays.

  • Township assessor: explains how your assessment was determined. The phone number is on the back of the tax bill.
  • Supervisor of Assessments, (630) 553-4146: assessment, property description, multiplier and exemption questions, and clerk to the Board of Review.
  • County Clerk, (630) 553-4104: tax rates and tax levies.
  • County Collector (Treasurer), (630) 553-4124: billing and payment.

A mailing name or address on the bill is corrected with the Change of Address form, mailed to the assessment office.

sections.h2: How does Kendall County assess homes?
sections.html:
Kendall County property outside farmland is assessed at a 33.33 percent median level of fair cash value, and the 2026 valuation date was January 1, 2026, using sales from 2023, 2024 and 2025. The county tax bill is the equalized assessed value minus exemptions, multiplied by the current tax rate.

Nine townships make up the county: Big Grove, Bristol, Fox, Kendall, Lisbon, Little Rock, Na-Au-Say, Oswego and Seward. Equalization factors are applied so each township reaches the required level.

The county's own test for over-assessment is to divide your assessment by the median level of assessment. If the result is above the estimated fair cash value, you may be over-assessed.

sections.h2: What is the process to contest a Kendall County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with your township assessor, then file a written complaint with the Board of Review inside 30 days of publication. The 2026 final filing date was October 19, 2026, and the filing window closes on the 30th day after publication for each township each year.

The Board of Review has three members appointed by the County Board, and each member must pass a state examination. The board reviews assessments made by township assessors, adds omitted property, hears complaints, and can raise or lower an assessment on its own motion. It also equalizes assessments between townships and reviews petitions for tax exemption, then passes its list of valuations to the County Clerk to compute tax rates. Complaint forms, instructions and the board's rules for 2026 are available by calling (630) 553-4146.

sections.h2: When are Kendall County tax bills due and what is the penalty?
sections.html:
Kendall County mails one tax bill in May, payable in two equal installments, and it does not send a second bill when the second installment comes due. Interest of 1.5 percent a month runs on any installment left unpaid past its due date.

  • Failure to receive a bill, or receiving it late, does not cancel the duty to pay or the penalties.
  • A $10.00 fee is added to the delinquent notice mailed after the second installment.
  • A returned check carries a minimum $25.00 charge and the payment is voided.
  • The county does not mail the original bill to a mortgage company, so an owner should ask the lender whether it needs a copy.
  • A duplicate bill is free to the owner, and non-owners pay $5.00.

Payments on the wrong parcel cannot be refunded automatically. Ask the Collector at (630) 553-4124 for the installment dates printed on your bill.

sections.h2: How do I protest a Kendall County tax bill?
sections.html:
To protest a bill, pay the tax in full and file a tax objection complaint with the Kendall County Circuit Clerk, and then the tax counts as paid under protest. No protest form or note on the bill is needed at the time of payment.

The Treasurer's protest letter sets two clocks, both counted from the first penalty date of the second installment. Full payment is due by day 60, and the complaint by day 75. For the 2025 tax year the letter gives November 9, 2026 for payment and November 24, 2026 for the complaint. The Circuit Clerk's fee is $119.00 for the first parcel and $50.00 for each added parcel. An objection to the assessed value requires that you first filed an assessment complaint with the Board of Review, and a filing with the state Property Tax Appeal Board for the same year blocks it. The letter notes that the Kendall County tax sale has generally been held in late October, so full payment must come before the sale to keep a property off it.

sections.h2: Which exemptions does Kendall County offer?
sections.html:
The assessment office lists homestead programs with dollar amounts as printed on its page, and says a driver's license must show the property address to receive any homestead exemption. Ask the office for current amounts before relying on any figure.

  • General Homestead Exemption: up to $6,000 on the increase above the 1977 value. Apply once while ownership and residency stay the same.
  • Home Improvement Exemption: up to $75,000 of added value for four years, certified by the township assessor with no application.
  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption: a $5,000 reduction for owners 65 or older, with a yearly renewal form mailed by the office.
  • Senior Assessment Freeze: household income cap of $65,000, yearly application, due on or before September 1.
  • Returning Veterans: a $5,000 reduction for two consecutive years.
  • Disabled Veterans' Standard Exemption: $2,500 for a 30 to 49 percent rating, $5,000 for 50 to 69 percent, and the first $250,000 of assessed value exempt at 70 percent or more.
  • Disabled Persons: a $2,000 reduction, with an annual application.

Religious, charitable and educational groups apply for non-homestead exemption through the Board of Review.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Kendall County housing?
sections.html:
Kendall County has 49,053 housing units and 45,372 households, and owners hold 84.0 percent of homes. Over 2020 to 2024 the typical owner-occupied home was valued at $322,400, and median gross rent was $1,781.

Median household income is $111,601, with owner costs of $2,264 a month with a mortgage and $1,001 without. Workers spend a mean of 31.6 minutes getting to work, and building permits totaled 733 in 2025. A seller can use the county's tax bill search to check the amount owed on a parcel before listing. The Collector at (630) 553-4124 can confirm what is unpaid.

sections.h2: What local details affect a Kendall County sale?
sections.html:
The northern half of the county falls in Community College District 516, served by Waubonsee Community College in Sugar Grove, Aurora and Plano, and the southern half is in District 525 with Joliet Junior College. Interstate 88 and Interstate 55 improved commuting to Chicago after World War II and fed the suburban growth that followed.

Silver Springs State Fish and Wildlife Area is the only designated state park in the county. A rural parcel can carry farmland assessments, which the 2026 notice increased by $56.71 per acre for each soil productivity index. Ask the township assessor which class your land is in.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Kendall County?
faqs.a: The Kendall County Collector bills and collects, at 504 S. Main St in Yorkville, phone (630) 553-4124. Tax rate and levy questions go to the County Clerk at (630) 553-4104.

faqs.q: How is Kendall County property tax split into installments?
faqs.a: One bill is mailed in May and payable in two equal installments. No second bill is sent, and unpaid installments accrue 1.5 percent interest per month.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 deadline to appeal a Kendall County assessment?
faqs.a: The final filing date for 2026 assessed values was October 19, 2026. Complaints must be filed in writing with the Board of Review within 30 days after publication.

faqs.q: Can I pay Kendall County taxes under protest?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the full tax within 60 days of the second installment's first penalty date and file a tax objection complaint with the Circuit Clerk within 75 days. The Clerk's fee is $119.00 for the first parcel.

faqs.q: Does Kendall County offer a senior assessment freeze?
faqs.a: Yes. It applies to owners 65 or older with household income of $65,000 or less, and the application is due on or before September 1 each year.
